newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam seeks 0.5-pct diesel for new power station.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam seeks 0.5-pct diesel for new power station.

text.p: Vietnam has started seeking one cargo per month of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil in preparation for the start up of a new diesel-fired power plant at Ho Chi Minh City in October, a trading source in Hanoi said on Tuesday.

The source said state-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) was seeking for the first time one 23,000-tonne cargo a month as part of its tender for October-December product requirements.
The tender, which closes on September 27, seeks a total of 261,000 tonnes of diesel and includes fuel oil and gasoline.
Vietnam normally buys 1.0-percent sulphur diesel and this will remain the main grade for transportation. There are no firm plans to switch to the 0.5 percent grade, the source said.
Another power station, the Tra Noc power station southeast of Ho Chi Minh City, is due to start up by March 1997.
The source said the power station was assessing whether to use diesel, gas or condensate for generation.
If this power station was to decide to use diesel, which is the most convenient fuel for generation, Petrolimex would need to import more 0.5 percent sulphur diesel next year, he said.
But in order to use gas, Vietnam would need pipelines to channel it from the offshore fields to the power station.
If the choice is to use condensate, the main importer would be Saigon Petro instead of Petrolimex, which is not a regular condensate importer, he said.
